name: PL/SQL
certifications: Oracle Database PL/SQL Developer Certified Professional (1Z0-149)

beginner.summary: For developers and analysts who know basic SQL and are new to PL/SQL. Covers a local Oracle Database Free lab, block structure, datatypes, control flow, SQL in PL/SQL, cursors, exceptions, procedures, functions, packages, collections, triggers, transactions, compiler warnings and dictionary views, finishing with an order management package.
prerequisites: Writes SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE statements with joins and GROUP BY
Understands tables, primary keys, foreign keys and constraints
Has a laptop that can run Docker or a cloud Oracle free-tier database, and uses a terminal confidently
outcomes: Write, compile and debug PL/SQL blocks, procedures, functions and packages
Process rows with cursors, records and collections and handle errors with exceptions
Control transactions and write audit triggers
Deliver a tested package with install and test scripts in Git

SQL*Plus settings: SET SERVEROUTPUT ON, SET LINESIZE and SHOW ERRORS

intermediate.summary: For developers who write basic PL/SQL and now need production-grade code. Covers bulk processing, REF cursors, pipelined functions, dynamic SQL and DBMS_SQL, autonomous transactions, error logging, compound triggers, definer's and invoker's rights, conditional compilation, package state, utPLSQL testing with coverage, PL/Scope, profiling, SQL macros, JSON and LOBs.
prerequisites: Completed the beginner level or can write packages, cursors, collections and exception handlers
Reads execution output and SQL timing from SQLcl
Can run Git and a container database locally
outcomes: Process millions of rows with BULK COLLECT, FORALL and pipelined functions
Write dynamic SQL, loggers and triggers that behave correctly under error
Test PL/SQL with utPLSQL and measure coverage and hot spots
Work with JSON and LOB data in PL/SQL

advanced.summary: For senior PL/SQL developers and technical leads. Covers memory and collection design, object types, generic programming, injection defence, fine-grained access control, least-privilege code, Advanced Queuing, scheduler and parallel execution, concurrency, edition-based redefinition, Oracle 23ai features including duality views, vector search and JavaScript in the database, application integration, production troubleshooting, refactoring, CI/CD and API design.
prerequisites: Completed the intermediate level or has two years of PL/SQL experience
Has written tests with utPLSQL and profiled code
Has Docker and Git and can read SQL trace output
outcomes: Use queues, jobs, locks and editions for safe concurrent releases
Apply Oracle 23ai JSON, vector and MLE features from PL/SQL
Automate tests and deployment in a CI/CD pipeline
